question.text: The order of the differential equation of the family of curves <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>d</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>e</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is (where, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>b</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>e</mi></math> are arbitrary constants)

solution.text:
We can re-write the equation of the curve as
y=a⋅3c⋅3bx+dsinx+e
or y=k⋅3bx+dsinx+e (where, k is an arbitrary constant)
As there are ‘4’ such constants, hence the order of the differential equation will be ‘4’
